title: Technical deep dive: Llama / Mistral / Qwen tuning (RoPE & MoE routing)
topics: Runtime performance: latency and throughput tradeoffs
KV cache behavior and warm/cold effects
Quantization impacts (4-bit vs int8) on latency and quality
MoE routing costs and gating overhead
RoPE scaling for long context lengths
summary: Deep technical session on per-model tuning for latency and throughput (Llama/Mistral/Qwen). Discussed KV cache sensitivity, batching, quantization tradeoffs, MoE routing overheads, and RoPE scaling. Agreed on next steps: run KV-sensitivity benchmarks, share rope-scaling spreadsheet, provide preliminary cost for Dedicated pilot and SOC2/KMS docs for private deployment.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, 60-70 minutes. agenda is runtime perf and model-specific tuning — Llama, Mistral, Qwen, plus MoE and RoPE behavior. intro quick round.
[00:12] Marco Santoro: Marco here — ML eng. we'll be doing a mix of Llama 2 variants and a few Mistral models in prod, also evaluating some Qwen. main pain is tail latency when context goes to 8k+ and cost for MoE.
[00:25] Priya Rao: great, thanks Marco. quick question — can you share your typical seq length distribution so we can prioritize rope tuning?
[00:33] Lena Wu: yea, I can share; median is ~512 but long tail to 12k, about 3% of requests.
[00:42] Jordan Lee: just to set expectations, RoPE scaling for 12k will hit both kernel memory and kv cache behavior; depending on chunking we may need custom kv handling.
[00:55] Oscar Diaz: our compliance folks also want to look at private deploy options — VPC + KMS. we'll want SOC2 docs.
[01:04] Ethan Kim: yes we'll share SOC2 and private deployment guide. ok start with runtime perf — Priya?
[01:10] Priya Rao: sure. high level: latency = f(model, quantization, batching, kv hit rate). throughput is impacted by batching and multi-request packing. with continuous batching we try to keep short-latency SLOs by dynamic batch cutoffs. for Llama family, 4-bit quant helps cost but can add a slight decoding jitter; for some Mistral weights 4-bit quant causes more perf variance.
[01:36] Marco Santoro: is that the same for Qwen? we saw odd degeneration when moving to q4 and we had to retrain llm-int8 calibrations.
[01:44] Priya Rao: Qwen's larger rotary embedding constants mean quant interacts with rope scaling differently; we've seen token-level perplexity rise at long contexts if quantization noise hits the attention score precision. so it's model dependent.
[01:59] Jordan Lee: and MoE — the gating adds a routing step. that routing overhead is small at the op level but it serializes certain parts of the forward pass causing increased tail latency under small batches. if you have a lot of small requests, MoE can blow up p95.
[02:18] Marco Santoro: we expected more cost on MoE but didn't realize routing was a latency cliff under 1-2 token responses.
[02:26] Priya Rao: yep. mitigation: route-heavy models on dedicated pools where you can amortize gating costs across larger micro-batches, or use hybrid routing — send low-cost routes to dense variants for short queries.
[02:38] Ethan Kim: is that automated? can Redwood route by policy?
[02:41] Priya Rao: yes, smart routing can send requests by latency vs cost policy; we can set rules per route. we also fallback to dense variant automatically if the pool is saturated.
[02:50] Lena Wu: about KV cache — our experience is cold cache cold start hits like 3-4x tokens cost. can Redwood warm caches across requests?
[02:59] Jordan Lee: we do prefix and KV caching; but warming requires either traffic reuse or synthetic warming. for Helix's 3% long-tail, a targeted prefix cache (store recent long sequences) reduces rehydration. also key eviction policy matters — LRU vs TTL.
[03:18] Marco Santoro: do you have numbers?
[03:20] Priya Rao: for example, a 16k context Llama variant with warm KV cache sees 30-40% lower per-token latency vs cold; throughput doubles in steady-state. but the warm-up phase depends on session stickiness.
[03:35] Marco Santoro: sticky sessions aren't guaranteed in our current infra; we use short-lived ephemeral connections.
[03:41] Jordan Lee: then we recommend either client side session tokens to pin to same host or configure placement affinity on Dedicated. in Private, you can ensure locality through VPC peering and stable routing.
[03:55] Oscar Diaz: about rope — what is rope scaling breakage? we saw hallucinations when context window jumped.
[04:02] Priya Rao: RoPE (rotary positional embeddings) scaling issues arise when absolute position extrapolation goes beyond training regime. many models use RoPE with scaling factors; scaling strategies (e.g., linear vs inv-scaling) affect attention alignment at long positions. Qwen and Mistral variants differ in their RoPE implementation and config. for Qwen we often use scaling factor tweaks and a custom freq shift to reduce drift.
[04:27] Marco Santoro: is that safe to change at inference or needs fine-tune?
[04:31] Priya Rao: usually you can adjust RoPE scaling at inference time, but you must validate on held-out long-context prompts — sometimes it reduces coherence. we can run ab tests.
[04:41] Jordan Lee: also note checkpoint differences: Llama family forks have different base RoPE params, so a one-size-fits-all won't work.
[04:49] Marco Santoro: batching — what kind of gains should we expect? we currently batch at request level with 4-8.
[04:55] Priya Rao: batching improves throughput but can increase p95. continuous batching and micro-batching with deadline cutoffs give a good tradeoff. for their workload, where median seq length is 512 and a 3% long tail, a dynamic policy: fast-path for <1024 tokens with small batch cap, and slow path for long contexts on Dedicated pools, works well.
[05:15] Lena Wu: quantization — you mentioned 4-bit causes jitter and some quality drop. what's Redwood's recommendation?
[05:21] Priya Rao: start with q8_0 or int8 if you can tolerate less cost reduction; q4_a variants are promising but require evals. we provide a quantization recommendation engine that suggests per-model profiles based on eval sets you share.
[05:35] Marco Santoro: can we run those evals with our prompts?
[05:38] Ethan Kim: yes, send us the prompt set and we'll run automated regressions. we'll share the eval harness.
[05:43] Oscar Diaz: network concerns for private deploy — if we go on-prem, what are the KMS and audit capabilities?
[05:49] Jordan Lee: private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, SAML/SSO, and we export audit logs; also we can restrict egress. we'll share the private deployment checklist.
[06:01] Marco Santoro: a deeper question on MoE routing cost math — how do you estimate per-token cost including gating?
[06:07] Priya Rao: approximate: base dense cost + gating overhead + expert compute. gating is small gflop but has memory copies and synchronization; experts add compute only for selected tokens. on small batches gating overhead dominates, so per-token cost can be 1.5-3x dense for low-latency small-batch settings. on large micro-batches amortized, MoE can be 30-50% cheaper at similar quality.
[06:30] Lena Wu: so for our short responses we should avoid MoE?
[06:33] Priya Rao: either avoid or route short-chat to dense variant; for long generation tasks MoE shines.
[06:39] Marco Santoro: curious about kernel selection and compilation — do you do per-model kernel selection automatically?
[06:44] Priya Rao: yes, the runtime picks kernels based on model arch, sequence length hist, and hardware. we also do quant-specific kernels. we can produce a profile report for your model mix.
[06:56] Ethan Kim: let's talk a little about scheduling for the pilot dedicated cluster and what you'd like from Redwood.
[07:01] Oscar Diaz: cost estimate, SLA, and a plan for running a 2-week benchmark with our real traffic.
[07:07] Priya Rao: we'll prepare a preliminary estimate. action items: we will run KV-sensitivity benchmarks (Priya), share rope-scaling spreadsheet and recommended scaling params (Priya/Jordan), and provide SOC2/private deploy docs (Ethan).
[07:22] Marco Santoro: also we need a reproducible benchmark harness to run locally for the team.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: we'll share the harness and a sample workload generator — you can run on-prem or against Dedicated.
[07:32] Lena Wu: can you also include guidance on TTL/eviction for KV cache?
[07:36] Priya Rao: yes. recommendation: TTL for session history of 24 hours for sticky users, LRU for general traffic, pinned prefixes for known long sequences. we'll document.
